rotation.note: Operator override for this unattended run: the FULL books keyword set is used as seeds (3 core + all 22 flat keywords = 25 working keywords), not a date-rotated slice. The date (day-of-month 19) is still used for EMPHASIS ordering only: 19 mod 22 = 19 -> the query list leads at flat-list index 19 (AI textbook -> AI copyright authors -> AI book recommendation -> wrap to AI co-writing, AI book cover, ...). Because 2026-09-18 shipped four copyright/litigation-and-translation cards (Anthropic settlement claims, unredacted MS/NYT filings, literary translation, scholarly unbundling), copyright-litigation and literary-translation angles are deliberately pushed to the BACK of the queue today and product/workflow angles (textbooks, discovery, ereader features, audiobooks, kidlit, comics, marketing, self-pub tooling) get first-pass budget.

retrieval_hint.why: Plain `site:` WebSearch returns stale evergreen pages for these outlets; the published_time gate then kills most of them. Harvest each domain's RSS/Atom/news-sitemap first, keep items whose pubDate is inside the 336h (14-day) window, and only then run the WebSearch queries below to fill gaps.
retrieval_hint.youtube_feed_pattern: https://www.youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml?channel_id=<UC...> — resolve channel_id by fetching https://www.youtube.com/@<handle> and reading `channelId` / `og:url` in the HTML.
retrieval_hint.paywall_note: thebookseller.com, publishersweekly.com and janefriedman.com premium posts are frequently teaser-only. Keep them as candidates (headline + dek + published_time are verifiable) but flag mode=summary.
retrieval_hint.saturation_note: Copyright-litigation news (Anthropic settlement, NYT v. OpenAI/Microsoft, Authors Guild motions) has filled books cards on 09-09, 09-14, 09-15 and 09-18. Only accept a NEW litigation item if it is a genuinely new development, not another procedural update.
